# HSpanTimeline

> Timing rows for overlapping requests and nested execution spans.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.10.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HSpanTimeline` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-span-timeline>`.
- Constructor: `HearthSpanTimelineElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Diagrams.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HSpanTimeline.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- start/end share a numeric unit (ms by default). Bars encode timing offsets and duration, including overlap. parentId supplies indentation with cycle/depth protection, while input order is preserved. Native table headers and named buttons expose exact starts/durations/statuses. maxRows defaults to 200 (maximum 1000); invalid and excess spans are reported as omitted.

## Public API

spans: SpanItem[] · label, unit, selected, maxHeight: string · maxRows: number

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    spans: SpanItem[];
    label: string;
    unit?: string;
    selected?: string;
    maxRows?: number;
    maxHeight?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ spans: () => [], unit: "ms", maxRows: 200, maxHeight: "420px" }
```

### Events

select(string)

```ts
type Emits = {
    select: [
        id: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, span

Use `hearth-span-timeline::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface SpanItem {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    start: number;
    end: number;
    parentId?: string;
    status?: RunStatus;
}

export type RunStatus = "pending" | "running" | "success" | "error" | "skipped";
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HSpanTimeline } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HSpanTimeline label="Request timing" :spans="[{id:'req',label:'Request',start:0,end:120,status:'success'},{id:'db',parentId:'req',label:'Database',start:20,end:95,status:'success'},{id:'cache',parentId:'req',label:'Cache',start:25,end:40,status:'success'}]" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-span-timeline');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Request timing",
  "spans": [
    {
      "id": "req",
      "label": "Request",
      "start": 0,
      "end": 120,
      "status": "success"
    },
    {
      "id": "db",
      "parentId": "req",
      "label": "Database",
      "start": 20,
      "end": 95,
      "status": "success"
    },
    {
      "id": "cache",
      "parentId": "req",
      "label": "Cache",
      "start": 25,
      "end": 40,
      "status": "success"
    }
  ]
});

element.addEventListener('select', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
